newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill Shi'ite Moslem activists in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill Shi'ite Moslem activists in Pakistan.

text.p: Gunmen killed two Shi'ite Moslem activists in Sahiwal town in the central Pakistani province of Punjab on Wednesday, police said.
They said activists Syed Abid Hussain Bukhari and his son Hyder Abbas Bukhari, both lawyers, were attacked when they were going to local courts in Sahiwal, 170 km (106 miles) southwest of Lahore.
The two died instantly when two gunmen riding a motorcycle fired several bullets from an automatic weapon, police added.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack, which the police said seemed to be the latest in a series of tit-for-tat killings between rival militant groups from the majority Sunni and the minority Shi'ite sects of Islam.
More than 100 people have been killed this year in a surge of sectarian violence in the populous Punjab.
Sunni groups accuse predominantly Shi'ite neighbour Iran of financing Pakistani Shi'ite militants, while Shi'ites accuse Sunni Saudi Arabia of aiding Sunni militants.
